review_notes: I read the whole file and the Basic.lean definitions of `grading`, `grading_piece` and `grading_piece_eq_iSup`. I also read the sibling Grading/Unit.lean and the two downstream users of `map_assoc_grading_piece` and `grading_piece`. In the target file, only the imported `assoc_tmul` is used as a simp lemma, and I found no loop or competing-rule problem there. The one issue is the simp interface around `grading_piece`, which the file's own docstring says blocks tagging `map_assoc_grading_piece` as simp. I did not check which other simp calls in the repo would change if `grading_piece` lost its simp attribute. Every use of it I found is an explicit `rw` or `simpa only`, so I expect little breakage, but I could not run Lean to confirm. The finding is a design recommendation, not an observed simplifier failure.

findings.excerpt: This is not a simp lemma, since `grading_piece` already rewrites its left-hand side.
findings.problem: The canonical statement about the abstract graded pieces cannot be a simp lemma. The cause is the simp attribute on `BalancedTensorProduct.grading_piece` (Basic.lean). That lemma unfolds every `(grading G H).piece p` into `((G.tensorProduct H).piece p).map (mkQ R A)`. Simp therefore rewrites the left-hand side of `map_assoc_grading_piece`, which is `((GL).piece p).map assoc.toLinearMap`, into a non-canonical form first. For a nested grading, the inner `grading` is expanded as well, exposing `InternalGrading.tensorProduct` and `mkQ` plumbing. The `GL`/`GR` pieces are the abstract interface that users want to keep. The file's docstring admits the conflict. The same blocking applies to the sibling lemmas `map_lid_grading_piece` and `map_rid_grading_piece`, which also carry no simp attribute. The downstream code in DG/Module/TensorProduct/Associator.lean has to invoke the lemma by hand through `simpa only [hMN, hNP] using map_assoc_grading_piece G H I p`.
findings.proposed_change: Remove `@[simp]` from `grading_piece` in Grading/Basic.lean. It is only a definitional unfolding lemma, and the uses I found are all explicit `rw [grading_piece]`, `rw [grading_piece, ...]` or `exact BalancedTensorProduct.grading_piece ...`. Keep the abstract `.piece` as the normal form. Then tag `map_assoc_grading_piece` (and the lid/rid analogues) `@[simp]` so that the image of a total-degree piece under the associator simplifies directly to the reassociated piece. If the `grading_piece` simp attribute must stay, instead state the expanded form as the simp normal form and drop the misleading docstring remark.
findings.benefit: Simp goals involving `((GL).piece p).map assoc` would reduce to `(GR).piece p` directly. Abstract pieces would no longer be forced into `mkQ`-image form. The docstring workaround and manual `simpa only` invocations would no longer be needed, and the simp set would have a single canonical form for these pieces.

evidence.excerpt: (grading (𝒜 := 𝒜) G H).piece p = ((G.tensorProduct H).piece p).map (mkQ R A) := by
simpa only [hMN, hNP] using map_assoc_grading_piece G H I p
